title: Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management as post-Brumadinho tailings governance rail
summary: GISTM is encoded as a post-Brumadinho global correction rail: it creates a lifecycle standard around affected people, knowledge base, design/monitoring, governance roles, emergency response, and public disclosure. It is not encoded as proof of conformance.

status_history.note: Added as rev0026 impoundment/tailings correction rail.

subjects.name: Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management

claims.claim: Global Tailings Review identifies itself as co-convened by ICMM, UNEP, and PRI.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The GISTM page says the Standard applies to existing and to-be-built tailings facilities, is directed at operators, and aims at zero tolerance for human fatalities and zero harm to people and the environment.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The Standard is organized around six topic areas, 15 principles, and 77 auditable requirements, with glossary, consequence-classification tables, and role/review-document summary tables.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The GISTM topic areas include project-affected people, social/environmental/local context and site characterization, design/construction/monitoring, governance roles and independent reviews, emergency preparedness, and public disclosure.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: auditable requirements, governance roles, lifecycle requirements, public disclosure expectations
type_payload.outputs: standard document, topic areas, principles, requirements, consequence classification, implementation/conformance expectations
type_payload.limitations: Conformance and enforcement are separate; operator adoption and independent audit results require separate records.

handling_notes: Infrastructure records are correction rails, not guarantees of correction or safety.
Avoid implying that standards, portals, or case-study sites replace regulatory authority, engineering judgment, community consent, or emergency preparedness.

unknowns: No conformance/certification implementation records have been promoted.
The standard’s legal force varies by jurisdiction and operator; this record does not establish compliance.
next_actions: Add GTMI / conformance-protocol infrastructure and early conformance-audit records.
Build implementation-lag records for operators/jurisdictions when sourced.
